Computational Simulation Study

Abstract

This computational study used a simulation model to investigate the spread of an infectious disease.

A compartmental SIR model was used to simulate disease transmission under different scenarios.

Methods

The simulation was implemented in Python.

The model included susceptible, infected, and recovered populations.

Initial conditions were defined for the simulated population, and model parameters included transmission and recovery rates.

Multiple simulation scenarios were evaluated by varying the model parameters.

The numerical equations were solved computationally to generate the simulated epidemic trajectories.

Results

The simulation demonstrated differences in epidemic dynamics across the evaluated parameter settings.

Data Availability

The simulation results generated during this study are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.
